catalog_quote: 5.1 SYNCHRONY. The Northern Salawati dialects, like the Maˈya dialects, have two tones—High /³/ and Rise /¹²/—which contrast with toneless syllables. Tonal specification is again largely restricted to word‑final syllables, and toneless words take an optional epenthetic /‑o/ in prepausal position. [...] However, unlike Maˈya, there is no contrastive lexical stress in Northern Salawati; stress is predictably word‑final. In fact, most of the phonetically polysyllabic lexicon of Northern Salawati can be analysed as sesquisyllabic: the nucleus of most non‑final syllables is a non‑stress‑bearing underspecified vowel (represented here as /ə/), the realisation of which is determined by a combination of the vowel of the final syllable and the surrounding consonants. new_statements.rule_in_words: Salawati (Northern Salawati dialects Butlih, Tepin, Wail) is a tone language (High vs Rise vs toneless, tone confined to the word-final syllable) with no contrastive stress: stress falls predictably on the word-final syllable; non-final syllables mostly carry a reduced, non-stress-bearing underspecified vowel (sesquisyllabic word shape).
new_statements.exceptions: None in Arnold 2025 for Northern Salawati (for sister language Batta, Arnold 2026 says 'with a handful of exceptions'). Arnold's 2021 conference slides had flagged a possible non-final stress in a few Butlih words ([ˈawe] 'child', [ˈmaněn] 'mother' vs [əˈle] 'cave', [məˈnjǎt] 'empty') and a few words with tone on a non-final syllable (/nǎ-lo/ 'sky'); the 2025 peer-reviewed analysis states stress is predictable and final. Underspecified-vowel realisation varies with speech rate (fn.30).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement based on a 324/391-item lexical database, each word recorded 'in a range of different utterance contexts, to accurately determine the word-prosodic specification' (sec. 3); toneless words take optional prepausal epenthetic /-o/. Language is tonal; this is a tonal-with-stress statement (reading fixed-final chosen for the stress rule; alternative label 'tonal-with-stress-statement').
new_statements.identity_note: Arnold 2025 describes 'Northern Salawati' = the dialect chain across north Salawati island, from first-hand data on three dialects: Butlih (2019), Tepin (2023), Wail (2023); she presumes Fiat, Mucu, Rajau are the same. Kawit (south Salawati; the variety Remijsen 2001:27 equates with the old name 'Maden') has NO prosodic data. Glottolog made1253 'Salawati' [xmx] covers all of these; Batta (Batanta, sister of the Salawati chain, separately described in Arnold 2026 LD&C 20) is a different glottocode and also has predictable final stress. Remijsen's 2001 'Fiawat' wordlist is from a Northern Salawati (Butlih-area) village.

sources.note: Sec. 5.1 (AAM p.34): Northern Salawati (Butlih, Tepin, Wail) has two tones (High, Rise) vs toneless, restricted to final syllables; 'no contrastive lexical stress in Northern Salawati; stress is predictably word-final'; polysyllables mostly sesquisyllabic with non-stress-bearing underspecified /ə/ in non-final syllables. Table 25: contrastive stress N. Sec. 5.2.1 (p.41): 'today all Salawati-Batta varieties have predictable final stress'; 5.2.4: contrastive stress of Proto-Salawati-Batta lost.

sources.citation: Arnold, Laura. 2021. The tonal phonologies of three undocumented Raja Ampat languages. P-Workshop, University of Edinburgh, 5 March 2021 (slides, 48 pp; file 'FourRajaAmpatLanguages').
sources.note: Butlih Salawati slides: final syllables have tone, longer duration, greater intensity, full vowel contrasts; non-final syllables reduced. Raises 'Stress on non-final syllable?' with [əˈle] 'cave' vs [ˈawe] 'child', [məˈnjǎt] 'empty' vs [ˈmaněn] 'mother'; summary slide: 'Butlih Salawati – Lexical stress + lexical tone (cf. Maˈya)'. Preliminary; superseded by Arnold 2025 (no contrastive stress).

sources.citation: Arnold, Laura. 2026. Sketch grammars of Wauyai Maˈya and Batta: Two underdocumented languages of Raja Ampat. Language Documentation & Conservation 20: 1-51 (hdl 10125/74842).
sources.note: Describes Batta (sister of the Salawati chain, different glottocode): 'no contrastive lexical stress in Batta; with a handful of exceptions, stress is predictably word-final'. Mentions Salawati dialects (Tepin, Wail, Fiat, Rajau, Butlih; Kawit undescribed) but gives no separate stress statement for them.
